cohort: 130 patients with a previous cesarean scar and 101 patients with previous vaginal delivery who underwent in vitro fertilization-embryo transfer (IVF-ET)
finding: Elective single-embryo transfer (eSET) is a safe and effective strategy for patients with a previous cesarean section undergoing IVF, yielding similar pregnancy and neonatal outcomes to patients with previous vaginal delivery while reducing the risk of multiple pregnancies associated with double-embryo transfer (DET).
mod_finding: The mode of delivery for the subsequent pregnancy was not associated with embryo implantation or pregnancy outcomes in patients with a previous cesarean section who underwent IVF.
birth_weight: Neonatal birth weight was similar between groups, but lower in the DET group compared to the eSET group.
